# kayjs-ui

> kay components ported from @kaynooo/svelte and @kaynooo/solidjs. They ship as `.kay` sources that the app compiles as its own, and they are styled by the classes of one `theme.css`, which the app restyles from its own stylesheet. The set: buttons and icons, toasts, dialogs and a form dialog that calls a page's action, a sortable table, switches and segmented controls, inputs and selects, cards, badges, popovers and tooltips.

## Rules that are easy to get wrong

- Import each component by its `.kay` path: `import Button from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/button.kay'`. Types, `toast`, `attempt` and the defaults come from the package itself: `import { toast } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui'`.
- Components write no Tailwind utility, only the classes of `theme.css`. A rule of the app's on one of those classes restyles every instance; utilities passed through a component's `class` prop restyle one.
- A static page cannot pass functions, `JSX.Element` props or children to an island. Render Dialog, Popover, FormDialog, or a Table with a `@cell` or `@empty` block, a function `sortValue` or a function `rowKey` from a component of the app that is an island itself: one with an `on*` handler, a `ref`, a `bind:` or a value import from `'kay'`. The examples below are written as such components.
- `toast` only shows in the browser, called from an island. The server's copy of the toast list is shared by every request, so it stays empty. Render one `Toaster` and one `TooltipHost` in the root layout.
- An icon is either a slot name such as `'close'`, which the app's settings map to any icon set, or an icon imported from `~icons/<prefix>/<name>`. The default slots use Tabler, so the app installs `@iconify-json/tabler`.
- Dialog and FormDialog follow `open`. The parent sets it, then sets it back to false in `onClose`, which runs however the dialog closed. Their content renders only while they are open. A Popover the page opens through `open` is set back the same way, in `onToggle`.
- FormDialog calls the action with the form's `FormData`. The server reads it as a plain form post, so give each control the `name` of its field in the action's schema: numbers, booleans and lists are coerced from their text, and files and the honeypot come along.
- Messages about the app's data are its own, passed as props (`failure`, `message`, `label`). The only text the library holds is the English wording of its own buttons and titles: `Cancel`, `Delete`, `Deleting…`, `Saving…`, `Loading…` and `Confirm Deletion`.

## Setup

kayjs-ui is published as `@kaynooo/kayjs-ui` to `https://git.kaynooo.fr/api/packages/kaynooo/npm/`, beside kay. kay 0.4 or later, Tailwind v4 and `@iconify-json/tabler` are peer dependencies.

```sh
bun add @kaynooo/kayjs-ui @iconify-json/tabler
```

`src/app.css`, imported by the root `_layout.kay`, imports the theme right after Tailwind. kay collects the classes of the library's templates along with the app's own, so no `@source` line has to point into `node_modules`:

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/theme.css';
@source '../.kay/classes.txt';

@theme {
  --color-accent: #7aa2f7;
}
```

The theme's tokens are `@theme default`, so the app's `@theme` overrides any of them wherever it sits:

- Surfaces, darkest first: `mantle`, `canvas`, `surface0`, `surface1`.
- Hairlines: `surface2` and `overlay0`.
- Text: `text`, `overlay1` (the faintest), `subtext0` and `muted`.
- State: `accent`, `accent-hi` (its hover), `on-accent` (text on it), `success`, `warning`, `info` and `error`.
- Fills: `fill-hover`, `fill-danger` and `row-hover`.
- Chart series: `chart-1` to `chart-6`.

```kay
---
import Toaster from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/toaster.kay'
import TooltipHost from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/tooltip-host.kay'
import './app.css'
---
slot
Toaster
TooltipHost
```

## Settings

The icons the components draw come from slots, each named for what it means: `alert`, `back`, `chevron`, `close`, `delete`, `globe`, `info`, `play`, `plus`, `search`, `spinner`, `success`, `zoomFit`, `zoomIn`, `zoomOut`. The app replaces any of them through kay's library settings, spreading the defaults:

```ts
// kay.config.ts
export default defineConfig({ settings: { '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui': './src/ui-settings.ts' } })
```

```ts
// src/ui-settings.ts
import type { Settings } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui'
import { defaults } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui'
import close from '~icons/lucide/x'

const settings: Settings = { ...defaults, icons: { ...defaults.icons, close } }

export default settings
```

`kay check` checks this module against `Settings`. The server, the browser, `kay build` and `kay test` all render with it.

## Components

Each component spreads the other attributes it is given onto its root element, `id`, `aria-*` and `data-*` included. The exceptions: Toggle spreads them on its checkbox, Popover on its panel, and ConfirmDelete, FormField, FormDialog, Toaster and TooltipHost take none.

### Icon, Button, IconButton

- `Icon(icon="close")`: an `svg.icon`. It is decorative unless `label` names it for screen readers. `icon` is a slot or an imported `~icons` icon.
- `Button(label="Save" variant="accent" icon="plus")`:
  - `variant` is `default`, `accent` or `danger`.
  - `busy` shows a spinner in place of the icon and sets `aria-busy`; it does not disable the button.
  - `expanded` sets `aria-expanded`, for a button that opens a panel.
  - `type` defaults to `button`, so a button inside a form never submits it by accident: pass `type="submit"` to submit. Children render after `label`.
- `IconButton(icon="delete" label="Delete")`: an icon alone. `label` names it for screen readers and shows as its tooltip through TooltipHost. `size` is `xs`, `sm`, `md` or `lg`; `variant` is `solid`, `ghost`, `inline` or `danger`.

### toast and Toaster

```ts
import { attempt, toast } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui'

toast.success('Saved')
toast.error('Could not save')
toast.info('Copied')

// Resolves to what the call returned, or to undefined once it threw and `failure` was toasted.
const post = await attempt(() => publish({ id }), 'Could not publish')
```

A toast stays for four seconds, or until its close button is pressed. Its clock stops while the pointer rests on the toasts or focus is inside them, and goes on with the time it had left once both are gone. Toaster is a manual popover in the top layer, so toasts show above an open dialog.

### Dialog, ConfirmDelete

```kay
Dialog(open={editing()} title="Rename" onClose={() => editing.set(false)})
  @footer
    Button(label="Cancel" onClick={() => editing.set(false)})
    Button(label="Rename" variant="accent" onClick={rename})
  input.field-input(name="name")
```

- Dialog is a modal `dialog`. It closes when its parent sets `open` to false, on Escape, or on a click outside. `onClose(event)` runs however it closed. Closed by Escape or a click outside, its content is still there to read; closed by the parent, it is already gone. Its title names it for screen readers.
- Once something has been typed inside, or while `dirty` is set (for example while a request is in flight), Escape and a click outside leave it open: only its own buttons close it.
- `ConfirmDelete(message="Delete this post?" failure="Could not delete" onConfirm={remove})` renders a trigger that opens a dialog asking before deleting:
  - While the promise `onConfirm` returns is pending, the dialog's buttons are disabled.
  - Once it resolves, the dialog closes. If it throws, `failure` is toasted and the dialog stays open.
  - `trigger="button"` makes the trigger a labelled danger button rather than an icon. `label` renames the trigger, for "Revoke link" or "Empty trash", and `class` goes on it. `size` and `variant` style the icon trigger only.

### Table

```ts
import type { Column } from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui'

const columns: Column<Post>[] = [
  { key: 'title', header: 'Title', sortValue: true, cell: true },
  { key: 'views', header: 'Views', sortValue: post => post.views, defaultDirection: 'desc', align: 'end' },
  { key: 'author', header: 'Author' },
]
```

```kay
Table(columns={columns} rows={posts} rowKey="id")
  @cell(post, column)
    a(href={`/posts/${post.id}`}) {post.title}
  @empty
    EmptyState(title="No posts yet")
```

- A column shows the row's value at `key` as text. With `cell: true`, it shows what the `@cell(row, column)` block draws instead.
- A column with `sortValue` sorts when its header is clicked. `true` sorts by the row's value at `key`; a function sorts by what it returns.
- The first click sorts in `defaultDirection`, `desc` unless set, and the next click flips it. `sort` gives the sort to start from.
- `serverSort` leaves the rows in the order they came. The headers show the sort, and `onSort(sort)` lets the page fetch the rows sorted that way, from a load or an action.
- With `sortValue: true`, dates sort by time, booleans as 0 and 1, and a missing value sorts last in either direction.
- `rowKey` is a field of the row or a function of it, and tells rows apart across a sort.

### Segmented, TabNav, Toggle

- `Segmented(options={[{ value: 'day', label: 'Day' }, { value: 'week', label: 'Week' }]} value="day" label="Period" name="period" onChange={period.set})`: real radios, so arrow keys move between options and the group posts as `name` inside a form. A parent passing another `value` moves the choice. `name` is required for now, until kay gives components a unique id.
- `TabNav(links={[{ href: '/settings', label: 'Profile' }, { href: '/settings/keys', label: 'Keys' }]} current={ctx.url.pathname} label="Settings")`: tabs as links, one page each. The current tab is marked `aria-current="page"`, and a bar too narrow for every tab scrolls to centre it, without moving the page.
- `Toggle(label="Public" checked={post.public} name="public" onChange={setPublic})`: a checkbox drawn as a switch, with `role="switch"`, that posts like a checkbox. Without `label`, give it `aria-label`.

### TextInput, Select

- `TextInput(value={title()} onInput={title.set} onChange={save})`:
  - `onInput(value)` runs on each keystroke, and `onChange(value)` once the value is committed, on blur or Enter.
  - A number box partway through a number, such as `1,`, reports nothing until it parses. A parent writing back its own spelling of the same number leaves the caret alone.
- `Select(value={kind()} options={[{ value: 'post', label: 'Post' }]} onChange={kind.set} emptyOption="Any")`:
  - `emptyOption` adds a first option worth `''`, labelled by the string, or blank with `true`.
  - `loading` shows a disabled row saying `loadingLabel` while the options are on their way.
  - The right option stays chosen when the options arrive after the value.

### Card, Badge, EmptyState

- `Card(title="Traffic")`: a `section.card` that frames its children in `.card-body`. `head` sits at the far end of the title's line, for a count or a link. `bare` drops the body's inset, for content that runs to the edge, such as a table.
- `Badge(label="Draft" tone="warning" icon="info")`: `tone` is `neutral`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` or `info`. Children render after `label`.
- `EmptyState(title="No posts yet" description="Write the first one.")`: what a list shows when it holds nothing.

### Popover, TooltipHost

```kay
Popover(id="post-menu" placement="bottom-end")
  @trigger(attributes)
    IconButton({...attributes} icon="chevron" label="More")
  Button(label="Duplicate" onClick={duplicate})
```

- Popover is the browser's popover. A click on the trigger toggles it, and a click outside or Escape closes it. `id` must be unique on the page, since it pairs the panel with its trigger, and made of letters, digits, `-` and `_`, since it also names the CSS anchor.
- `@trigger(attributes)` renders the trigger, which spreads `attributes`: `popovertarget`, `aria-expanded` and its anchor.
- `placement` is `bottom-start`, `bottom-end`, `top-start` or `top-end`, and the browser flips it when there is no room.
- `open` opens or closes it from the page, and `onToggle(open)` runs however it changed: a page driving `open` sets its own value back there, or it could not open the panel again after a click outside closed it.
- TooltipHost shows the `data-tooltip` of whichever element the pointer or a tab lands on. `data-tooltip-placement`, a CSS `position-area`, says where it sits, `top` by default: `button(data-tooltip="Copy link" data-tooltip-placement="bottom")`. IconButton sets `data-tooltip` to its label.

## Forms

FormField frames a control with its label, hint and messages. FormDialog calls a page's action from a dialog and shows the message of each refused field on its FormField.

```kay
--- server
import { t } from 'elysia'
import { action } from 'kay'

export const rename = action(t.Object({ id: t.String(), title: t.String({ minLength: 2, error: 'Two letters at least' }) }), async ({ id, title }) => posts.rename(id, title))
---
```

```kay
---
import { signal } from 'kay'
import Button from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/button.kay'
import FormDialog from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/form-dialog.kay'
import FormField from '@kaynooo/kayjs-ui/form-field.kay'
import { rename } from '../routes/posts/[id].kay'

const { post } = props<{ post: Post }>()

const editing = signal(false)
const title = signal(post.title)
---
Button(label="Rename" onClick={() => editing.set(true)})
FormDialog(open={editing()} title="Rename" action={rename} submitLabel="Rename" failure="Could not rename" onSaved={saved => title.set(saved.title)} onClose={() => editing.set(false)})
  input(type="hidden" name="id" value={post.id})
  FormField(label="Title" name="title" required)
    input.field-input(name="title" value={title()})
```

- FormDialog calls `action` with `new FormData(form)`, read on the server as a plain form post and answered as a call. An action that redirects takes the browser there instead.
- When the action refuses a field, its message shows on the FormField with that `name`, and the dialog stays open.
- A refused message no FormField shows is toasted instead, a refusal of the whole form under the empty name included. A failure carrying no message toasts `failure`.
- A save hands what the action returned to `onSaved`, then closes the dialog.
- The submit button sits in the footer, paired with the form by `id`. The `id` defaults to one named after the action, so give one when two dialogs on a page call the same action.
- Enter submits from a single-line field, and Ctrl+Enter from a textarea. While the call is under way, the buttons are disabled, and Escape or a click outside leaves the dialog open.
- `extra` fills the left end of the footer, for a ConfirmDelete with `trigger="button"`.

FormField also works outside a dialog, in a plain form posting to an action:

- `issue` shows a message of the page's own, such as `ctx.failed(rename)?.errors.title`.
- `hint` explains the control, under it. `action` sits at the end of the label's line. `required` marks the label with a `*` hidden from screen readers, which read the control's own `required`.
- The label holds only the label's text and the control, so the hint, the messages and the action stay out of the control's accessible name.
- `group` makes it a `fieldset` with a `legend`, for a control made of several inputs.
- Its messages sit in an `aria-live` region, so a screen reader reads them as they appear.

## Testing an app's use of it

A page that uses the components renders them in `testSite()` like the app's own. To test what their handlers do, `mount(file, props)` from `kay/test` renders a component of the app, once a DOM is registered, such as with `GlobalRegistrator.register()` from `@happy-dom/global-registrator`. happy-dom has no popover API, so Toaster and Popover need a shim of `showPopover`, `hidePopover`, `togglePopover` and `:popover-open` there.
